Rounded to the **nearest tenth of a degree**, $m∠B≈${{field-1}}${}^{∘}.$
question.worked_solution:
We use the Law of Cosines to solve for angle $B:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡B & =\frac{{a}^{2}+{c}^{2}-{b}^{2}}{2ac}.\end{aligned}
$$

 
Here, we have

$$
a=9,\,b=6,\,c=7.
$$

This gives 

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡B & =\frac{{9}^{2}+{7}^{2}-{6}^{2}}{2(9)(7)} \\  & =\frac{81+49-36}{126} \\  & =\frac{94}{126} \\  & =\frac{47}{63}.\end{aligned}
$$

 
Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠B & =\operatorname{arccos}⁡(\frac{47}{63}) \\  & ≈{41.8}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to the nearest tenth.
